hypotheses.reasoning: audit-consumer is stuck on one malformed message, msg-273662, at audit.events partition 0 offset 584855. Parsing fails with 'Unexpected token \u0000 in JSON at position 1436' (#1069, #1171, #1303). The consumer nacks and redelivers it with no max-retries or dead-letter route (#1070, #1172, #1305: attempts 7, 10, 14). Because partition 0 is ordered, every later message waits behind it, so lag climbs from 629 messages/57s (#1211) to 5204 messages/228s (#1567). CPU stays normal because the consumer is blocked on retries, not computing. The account-svc 120s confirmation timeouts (#1259, #1367, #1578) are downstream effects of the audit pipeline backing up, not the origin. The billing-reconciler checksum errors on invoice_archive rows (#559, #668, etc.) are a separate data-integrity issue in an unrelated archive partition and do not touch audit.events. The slow seq-scan on accounts-db audit_log (#140) is a minor side issue.

Corrupt records exist in billing-reconciler invoice_archive (checksum violations in 2019 partitions). This is a plausible but unlikely cause of the audit lag, since those errors come from a different service and table and are skipped, not blocking. Only the audit.events lag matches the alert.

verdict.recommendedAction: Move msg-273662 (audit.events partition 0, offset 584855) to a dead-letter queue so the partition can drain, then resume audit-consumer. Find the producer that wrote the NUL byte into the payload and fix its serialization or sanitize input. Add a max-retry limit and DLQ routing to audit-consumer so one bad message cannot block a partition again. Investigate the invoice_archive checksum violations in billing-reconciler (2019-Q1..Q4 partitions) as a separate issue.
